(a) Purpose and intent. The purpose of this article is to protect the public health, safety, environmental and general welfare through the regulation of non-stormwater discharges to the municipal separate storm sewer system to the maximum extent practicable as required by federal law. This article establishes methods for controlling the introduction of pollutants into the municipal separate storm sewer system in order to comply with requirements of the National Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) permit process. The objectives of this article are to:
(1) Regulate the contribution of pollutants to the municipal separate storm sewer system by any person;
(2) Prohibit illicit discharges and illegal connections to the municipal separate storm sewer system;
(3) Prevent non-stormwater discharges, generated as a result of spills, inappropriate dumping or disposal; to the municipal separate storm sewer system; and
(4) To establish legal authority to carry out all inspection and enforcement procedures necessary to ensure compliance with this article.
(b) Applicability. The provisions of this article shall apply to the unincorporated area of Floyd County.
(c) Compatibility with other regulations. This article is not intended to modify or repeal any other [article], ordinance, rule, regulation, [or] other provision of law. The requirements of this article are in addition to any other ordinance, rule regulation, or other provision of law and where this any provision of this article imposes restrictions different from those imposed by any other ordinance, rule regulation, or other provision of law, whichever provision is more restrictive or imposes higher protective standards for human health or the environment shall control.
(d) Severability. If the provisions of any section, subsection, paragraph, subdivision or clause of this article shall be adjudged invalid by a court of competent jurisdiction, such judgment shall not affect or invalidate the remainder of any section, subsection, paragraph, subdivision or clause of this article.
(e) Responsibility for administration. The public works director shall administer, implement, and enforce the provisions of this article.
(Ord. No. 2006-007A, § 1, 12-12-06)

(a) Prohibition of illicit discharges. No person shall throw, drain, or otherwise discharge, cause, or allow others under its control to throw, drain, or otherwise discharge into the municipal separate storm sewer system any pollutants or waters containing any pollutants, other than stormwater. The following discharges are exempt from the prohibition provision above:
(1) Water line flushing, other potable water sources, landscape irrigation or lawn watering, individual residential and non-commercial car washing, de-chlorinated swimming pool water, street wash water, diverted stream flows, rising ground water, ground water infiltration to storm drains, uncontaminated pumped ground water, foundation or footing drains, crawl space pumps, air conditioning condensation, springs, natural riparian habitat or wetland flows, and any other water source not containing pollutants;
(2) Discharges or flows from fire fighting, and other discharges specified in writing by the public works director as being necessary to protect public health and safety;
(3) The prohibition provision above shall not apply to any non-stormwater discharge permitted under an NPDES permit or order issued to the discharger and administered under the authority of the state and the Federal Environmental Protection Agency, provided that the discharger is in full compliance with all requirements of the permit, waiver, or order, and other applicable laws and regulations, and provided that written approval has been granted for any discharge to the municipal separate storm sewer system.
(b) Prohibition of illegal connections. The construction, connection, use, maintenance, or continued existence of any illegal connection to the municipal separate storm sewer system is prohibited.
(1) This prohibition expressly includes, without limitation, illegal connections made in the past, regardless of whether the connection was permissible under laws or practices applicable or prevailing at the time of the connection.
(2) A person violates this article if the person connects a line conveying sewage to the municipal separate storm sewer system, or allows such a connection to continue.
(3) Improper connections in violation of this article must be disconnected and redirected, if necessary, to an approved onsite wastewater management system or the sanitary sewer system upon approval of the water and sewer division.
(4) Any drain or conveyance that has not been documented in plans, maps, or equivalent, and which may be connected to the storm sewer system, shall be located by the owner or occupant of that property upon receipt of written notice of violation from the public works director requiring that such locating be completed. Such notice will specify a reasonable time period within which the location of the drain or conveyance is to be completed, that the drain or conveyance be identified as storm sewer, sanitary sewer, or other, and that the outfall location or point of connection to the storm sewer system, sanitary sewer system or other discharge point be documented and provided to the public works department.

448:
(a) Violations. It shall be unlawful for any person to violate any provision or fail to comply with any of the requirements of this article. Any person who has violated or continues to violate the provisions of this article, may by subject to the enforcement actions outlined in this section, restrained by injunction, or otherwise penalized in a manner provided by law.
(b) Notice of violation and order of abatement. Whenever the public works director or his designated representatives find any violations of this Code or any indicators of a potential violation, as defined in this Code, they are authorized to issue or serve a written notice of the findings of an inspection as set forth in this section.
(1) Abatement order—Written. Whenever the public works director or his designated representatives find any violations of this Code, they are authorized to issue a written order to correct or abate the violations. Such order when issued shall set forth a reasonable and realistic timeframe or date limit for correction, abatement or compliance. The timeframe for correction, abatement or compliance established by or as directed by the public works director or his designated representative may be reasonably correlated by him to the seriousness or relative degree of violation, and or to the complexity of the means of correction or abatement.
(2) Same—Verbal. Where deemed necessary, due to the potential threat or danger to persons or property, the public works director may issue a verbal order for the immediate correction or abatement of a violation or fire hazard. This may be followed by a written order.
(3) Serving notices or orders. The service of notices or orders may be made by the public works director or his representatives upon the owner, occupant, or person in charge of the building, structure, facility, premises or portion thereof where the violations or indicators of a potential violation were found, or be delivering a copy of the notice or order to any or all of the persons noted. If such person cannot be served as noted, service may be accomplished by affixing a copy of the notice or order in a conspicuous place at or near the entrance of the building, structure, facility or premises, or by delivering or sending a copy of the notice or order to the known agent of the owner or occupant, or in the event of an absentee owner with no known agent, by sending a copy by certified or registered mail to the owner's last known residence, business or post office address.
(4) Same—To occupants of certain premises. If the building, structure, facility or premises is owned by one (1) or more persons and is occupied by one (1) or more other persons under lease or otherwise, the notice or order issued in connection with this section shall apply to the occupants thereof, except where the notice or order requires the addition to or changes in the building, structure, or premises such as would immediately become real estate and becomes the property of the owners and not the occupants unless it is otherwise agreed between or among the owners and the occupants.
(c) Appeal of notice or order. Any person receiving a notice of violation or order of abatement may appeal the determination of the public works director. The notice of appeal must be received within fifteen (15) days from the date of the notice of violation or order of abatement. Hearing on the appeal shall be conducted by the board of appeals and adjustments as provided in article 2.11 of the unified land development code.
(d) Enforcement measures.
(1) Jurisdiction. The municipal court shall have full jurisdiction to try and dispose of all questions of violations of this article and shall also have jurisdiction to try and, in case of conviction, to punish persons failing to abate violations, as prescribed in subsection (b).
(2) Abatement measures.
a. Non-emergency. In any case where the owner, agent or tenant fails to abate the violation in the time specified, or where the owner, agent or tenant cannot be served with notice, or where the nature of the violation is such, in the opinion of the judge, that it must be immediately abated, the judge may issue an order to the public works director directing the violation be abatement. The public work director, in such case, shall keep a record of the expenses and costs of abating same, and the costs shall be billed against the owner, agent or tenant for collection as for Floyd County revenues.
b. Emergency. The public works director shall have the authority to summarily abate any violation of this Code, which constitutes an emergency condition, as defined by this Code, and where following the provisions for obtaining corrective action or abatement as set forth elsewhere in this Code is not practical in his judgment. A record of expenses and costs and the recovery of those costs shall be as for a non-emergency abatement.
(3) Other Floyd County departments shall assist the public works department as is necessary in abating violations under this section.
(e) Cost of abatement of the violation. Within ninety (90) days after abatement of the violation, the owner of the property will be notified of the cost of abatement, including administrative costs. If the amount due is not paid within thirty (30) days after the receipt of the notice, the charges shall become a special assessment against the property and shall constitute a lien on the property for the amount of the assessment. Any persons violating any of the provisions of this article shall become liable to Floyd County by reason of this violation.
(f) Penalties; separate violations. Any person who shall fail to comply with an order of abatement as set forth in this section, or who shall act in violation of this Code or of any detailed statement of specifications or plans submitted and approved under authority of this Code in connection with any approval, certificate, or permit issued there under, or who shall perform any act deemed to create a serious potential for an illicit discharge or illegal connection and for which an issuance of an order to correct or abate is not adequate, and who is found guilty shall be guilty of a violation of this Code. A person found guilty under this section shall, for each violation and non-compliance, respectively, be subject to punishment by a fine of not less than one hundred dollars ($100.00) nor more than one thousand dollars ($1,000.00) or by imprisonment for a period of not more than one hundred twenty (120) days or by both such fine and imprisonment. The imposition of a penalty for any violation shall not excuse the violation or permit it to continue, and the responsible persons shall correct or abate such violation within a time limit as ordered by the court. When not otherwise specified, each day a prohibited condition or violation continues following an order of the court to correct or abate same shall constitute a separate offense.
(g) Violations deemed a public nuisance. In addition to the enforcement processes and penalties provided, any condition caused or permitted to exist in violation of any of the provisions of this article is a threat to public health, safety, welfare, and environment and is declared and deemed a nuisance, and may be abated by injunctive or other equitable relief as provided by law.
(h) Remedies not exclusive. The remedies listed in this article are not exclusive of any other remedies available under any applicable federal, state or local law and the public works director may seek cumulative remedies.
(Ord. No. 2006-007A, § 7, 12-12-06)

(a) Upon the declaration of a state of emergency by the governor, or upon the determination by the county governing authority, or its designee, of the existence of an emergency or disaster, the county governing authority, its designee or the emergency interim successor may adopt a resolution instituting a curfew when it is determined necessary to protect and safeguard the people and property of Floyd County.

The resolution may, in the discretion of the governing authority, also exempt regular employees of local industries traveling to and from their jobs with appropriate identification, news media employees, building and repair contractors, properly registered according to the Floyd County "Ordinance to Require Registration of Building and Repair Services During a State of Emergency"), performing activities related to construction, repair, renovation or improvement of buildings and other structures damaged during the disaster or emergency.
State of emergency. As defined by O.C.G.A. § 38-3-3, a condition declared by the governor when, in his judgment, the threat or actual occurrence of a disaster, emergency, or energy emergency is of sufficient severity and magnitude as to warrant extraordinary efforts in preventing or alleviating the damage, loss, hardship, or suffering threatened or caused thereby.
(Ord. No. 2011-003A, § 2, 2-22-11; Amend. of 2-28-12, § I)
461:

(Ord. No. 2011-003A, § 3, 2-22-11)

466:
Overcharging. The term "overcharging" is defined as charging prices for goods, materials, services, or housing which are substantially in excess of the customary charges or in applicable cases substantially in excess of the supplier's or provider's costs for such goods, materials, services or housing. The existence of overcharging shall be presumed from a substantial increase in the price at which the goods, materials, services, or housing was offered in the usual course of business immediately prior to the onset of the emergency, but shall not include increases in costs to the supplier directly attributable to higher costs of materials, supplies, and labor costs resulting from the emergency.
State of emergency. 470:
(a) Meetings. Such meetings may be called by the presiding officer or any two (2) members of the governing body without regard to or compliance with time-consuming procedures and formalities otherwise required by law.

County: The unincorporated area of this county.
Due date: From the twentieth day after the close of the monthly period for which tax is to be computed.
Guestroom: A room occupied, or intended, arranged or designed for occupancy, by one (1) or more occupants for the purpose of living quarters or residential use. It shall not include meeting rooms or exhibition halls.
Hotel: Any structure or any portion of a structure including any lodginghouse, roominghouse, dormitory, turkish bath, bachelor hotel, studio hotel, motel, motor hotel, auto court, inn, public club or private club, containing guestrooms and which is occupied or is intended or designed for occupancy by guests, whether rent is paid in money, goods, labor or otherwise. Monthly period: The calendar month of any year.
Occupancy: The use or possession, or the right to the use or possession, of any room or apartment in a hotel or the right to the use or possession of the furnishings or to the services and accommodations accompanying the use and possession of the room or apartment.

Person: As defined in section 2-1-2, except the United States of America, this state and any political subdivision of either thereof upon which the county is without power to impose the tax herein provided.
Rent: The consideration received for occupancy valued in money, whether received in money or otherwise, including all receipts, cash, credits and property or services of any kind or nature, and also the amount for which credit is allowed by the operator to the occupant, without any deduction therefrom whatsoever.
Return: Any return filed or required to be filed as herein provided.
Tax: The tax imposed by this article.

(a) Due date of taxes. All amounts of such taxes shall be due and payable monthly on or before the twentieth day of every month next succeeding each respective monthly period as defined in section 2-9-70.

Public authority means any member of a governing authority, any housing authority officer, or any officer who is in charge of any department or branch of the government of the municipality, county, or state relating to health, fire or building regulations or to other activities concerning dwellings, buildings; or structures in the county or municipality.

Repair means altering or improving a dwelling, building, or structure so as to bring the structure into compliance with the applicable codes in the jurisdiction where the property is located and the cleaning or removal of debris, trash, and other materials present and accumulated which create a health or safety hazard in or about any dwelling, building, or structure.
Resident means any person residing in the jurisdiction where the property is located on or after the date on which the alleged nuisance arose.
(Ord. of 8-9-16)
541:
(a) It is the duty of the owner of every dwelling, building, structure, or property within the jurisdiction to construct and maintain such dwelling, building, structure or property in conformance with applicable codes in force within the city, or such ordinances which regulate and prohibit activities on property and which declare it to be a public nuisance to construct or maintain any dwelling, building, structure or property in violation of such codes or ordinances. It shall be unlawful for such owner to allow a dwelling, building, structure, or property within the jurisdiction to become unsafe, unsanitary, dangerous or detrimental to the health, safety or welfare, or otherwise inimical to the welfare of the residents of the city or otherwise become a nuisance as set forth under this Code or the laws of this state.
(b) It is further the duty of the every owner and occupant of every dwelling, building, structure, or property within the jurisdiction to maintain safe and sanitary premises and not to create, maintain or allow the accumulation of weeds, brush, vegetation, trash, junk, debris, filth and other unsafe or unsanitary conditions on or in said dwelling, building, structure, or property. It shall be unlawful for such owner or occupant to create, maintain or allow such unsafe or unsanitary conditions on said dwelling, building, structure, or property.
(c) The Floyd County Board of Commissioners hereby appoints and designates the county code enforcement officer, city fire marshal, Floyd County Police Chief, and the Chief Building Inspector of the Rome/Floyd County Building Inspection Department and their respective designees, as public officers to exercise the powers prescribed by this article.
(d) Whenever a request is filed with the public officer by a public authority or by at least five (5) residents of Floyd County, charging that any dwelling, building, or structure is unfit for human habitation or for commercial, industrial, or business use and not in compliance with applicable codes; is vacant and being used in connection with the commission of drug crimes; or constitutes an endangerment to the public health or safety as a result of unsanitary or unsafe conditions, the public officer shall make an investigation or inspection of the specific dwelling, building, structure or property.
(1) If the officer's investigation or inspection identifies that any dwelling, building, structure or property is unfit for human habitation or for commercial, industrial, or business use and not in compliance with applicable codes; is vacant and being used in connection with the commission of drug crimes; or constitutes an endangerment to the public health or safety as a result of unsanitary or unsafe conditions, the public officer may issue a complaint in rem against the lot, tract, or parcel of real property on which such dwelling, building, or structure is situated or where such public health hazard or general nuisance exists and shall cause summons and a copy of the complaint to be served on the interested parties for such dwelling, building, or structure.
(2) The complaint shall identity the subject real property by appropriate street address and official tax map reference; identify the interested parties; state with particularity the factual basis for the action; and contain a statement of the action sought by the public officer to abate the alleged nuisance. The summons shall notify the interested parties that a hearing will be held before the Floyd County Magistrate Court at a date and time certain and at a place within the city where the property is located. Such hearing shall be held not less than fifteen (15) days nor more than forty-five (45) days after the filing of said complaint in court. The interested parties shall have the right to file an answer to the complaint and to appeal in person or by attorney and offer testimony at the time and place fixed for the hearing.
(3) Floyd County Magistrate Court shall have full jurisdiction to try and dispose of all such complaints.
(e) If after such notice and hearing, the court determines that the dwelling, building, or structure in question is unfit for human habitation or is unfit for its current commercial, industrial, or business use and not in compliance with applicable codes; is vacant and being used in connection with the commission of drug crimes; or constitutes an endangerment to the public health or safety as a result of unsanitary or unsafe conditions, the court shall state in writing findings of fact in support of such determination and shall issue and cause to be served, upon the interested parties that have answered the complaint or appeared at the hearing an order which:
(1) If the repair, alteration, or improvement of the said dwelling, building, or structure can be made at a reasonable cost in relation to the present value of the dwelling, building, or structure, requiring the owner, within the time specified in the order, to repair, alter, or improve such dwelling, building, or structure so as to bring it into full compliance with the applicable codes relevant to the cited violation and, if applicable, to secure the structure so that it cannot be used in connection with the commission of crimes; or
(2) If the repair, alteration, or improvement of the said dwelling, building, or structure in order to bring it into full compliance with applicable codes relevant to the cited violations cannot be made at a reasonable cost in relation to the present value of the dwelling, building, or structure, requiring the owner, within the time specified in the order, to demolish and remove, such dwelling, building, or structure and all debris from the property.
For purposes of this article, the court shall make its determination of "reasonable cost" in relation the present value of the dwelling, building or structure without consideration of the value of the land on which the structure is situated; provided, however, that costs of the preparation necessary to repair, alter, or improve a structure may be considered. The income and financial status of the owner shall not be factor in the court's determination. The present value of the structure and the costs of repair, alteration, or improvement may be established by affidavits of real estate appraiser's with a Georgia appraiser classification as provided in O.C.G.A. Title 41, Ch. 39A, qualified building contractor's, or qualified building inspectors without actual testimony presented. Costs of repair, alteration, or improvement of the structure shall be the cost necessary to bring the structure into compliance with the applicable codes relevant to the cited violations in force in the jurisdiction.
(f) If the owner fails to comply with an order to repair or demolish the dwelling, building, or structure, the public officer may cause such dwelling, building, or structure, to be repaired, altered, improved, to be vacated and closed, or demolished. Such abatement action by the county shall commence within three hundred (300) days after the expiration of time specified in the court order for abatement by the owner. Any time during which such action is prohibited by a court order issued pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 41-2-13 or any other equitable relief granted by a court of competent jurisdiction, shall not be counted toward the three hundred (300) days in which such abatement action must commence. The public officer shall cause to be posted on the main entrance of the building, dwelling, or structure a placard with the following words:
"This building is unfit for human habitation or commercial, industrial, or business use and does not comply with the applicable codes or has been ordered secured to prevent its use in connection with drug crimes or constitutes and endangerment to the public health or safety as a result of unsanitary or unsafe conditions. The use or occupation of this building is prohibited and unlawful."
(g) If the public officer has the structure demolished, reasonable effort shall be made to salvage reusable materials for credit against the cost of demolition. The proceeds of any moneys received from the sale of salvaged materials shall be used or applied against the cost of the demolition and removal of the structure, and proper records shall be kept showing application of sales proceeds. Any such sale of salvaged materials may be made without the necessity of public advertisement and bid. The public officer and the city are relieved of any and all liability resulting from or occasioned by the sale of any such salvaged materials, including, without limitation, defects in such salvaged materials.
(h) The public officer's designated herein may issue citations for violations of state minimum standard codes, optional building, fire, life safety, and other codes adopted by ordinance, and conditions creating a public health hazard or general nuisance, and may seek to enforce such citation in any court of competent jurisdiction prior to issuing a complaint in rem as provided in this article.
(i) In addition to any other power or authority granted in this article to the court, the court shall have full jurisdiction and authority to punish persons found to have created, allowed or maintained a nuisance or other dangerous, unsafe or unsanitary condition, and who have refused to abate the same, as provided for in section 1-9 of this Code.
(j) Nothing in this article shall be construed to impair or limit in any way the power of the county to define and declare nuisances and to summarily and without notice order the abatement of or abate any nuisance or dangerous condition where the case is an urgent one and the health and safety of the public or a portion thereof is in imminent danger.
(Ord. of 8-9-16)
542:
(a) The public officer may determine, under existing ordinances, that a dwelling, building, or structure is unfit for human habitation or is unfit for its current commercial, industrial, or business use if he/she finds that conditions exist in such building, dwelling, or structure which are dangerous or injurious to the health, safety, or morals of the occupants of such dwelling, building, or structure; of the occupants of neighborhood dwelling, buildings, or structures; or of other residents of the city. Such conditions include the following (without limiting the generality of the foregoing):
(1) Those buildings, dwellings or structures whose interior or exterior bearing walls, or other vertical structural members list, lean or buckle to such extent as to weaken the structural support of such member or members below the minimum required by the building codes of the city and/or county.
(2) Those buildings, dwellings or structures, which have improperly distributed loads upon the floors or roofs or in which the same are overloaded, or which have insufficient strength to be reasonably safe for the purpose for which it is used, or intended to be used.
(3) Those buildings, dwellings or structures, which have visible soil erosion adjacent to or under any structural support.
(4) Those buildings, dwellings or structures, which have parts that are so attached that they are likely to fall and injure persons or property.
(5) Those buildings, dwellings or structures, which are unfit for human habitation or for commercial, industrial, or business uses due to dilapidation and defects increasing the hazards of fire, accident or other calamities.
(6) Those buildings, dwellings or structures having inadequate facilities for egress in the event of a catastrophe, such as windstorm, fire, earthquake or panic because of inadequate stairways, elevators, escalators or fire escapes, such that such defect is likely to cause injury to persons or property in the event of such a catastrophe.
(7) Those buildings, dwellings or structures which, have been damaged by fire, wind or other causes so as to have become dangerous to life, safety or the general health and welfare of the occupants thereof or the people of the city.
(8) Those buildings, dwellings or structures which have become so dilapidated, decayed, damaged, unsafe, unsanitary, or which so utterly fail to provide the amenities essential to decent living such as effective and adequate ventilation, plumbing, sanitation facilities, running water, light or other facilities such that such conditions render the dwellings, buildings, or structure dangerous or detrimental to the health, safety, morals, or welfare of either those living therein, those who may live therein, or the people of the county.
(9) Those buildings, dwellings or structures where an accumulation of weeds, trash, junk, filth and other unsanitary or unsafe conditions shall create a public health hazard or general nuisance to those persons residing in the vicinity.
(10) Those buildings, dwellings or structures which exist in violation of any ordinances of the county such that said building, dwelling or structure is unfit for human habitation or is unfit for its current commercial, business or industrial use due to conditions existing in such building, dwelling or structure which are dangerous or injurious to the health, safety or morals of the occupants of such building, dwelling or structure, of the occupants of the neighborhood buildings, dwellings or structures, or of other residents of the county.
(11) Other additional standards which may from time to time be adopted and referenced herein by ordinance amendment.
(b) The public officer may determine, under existing ordinances, that a dwelling, building, or structure is vacant, dilapidated, and being used in connection with the commission of drug crimes based upon personal observation or report of a law enforcement agency and evidence of drug crimes being committed.
(Ord. of 8-9-16)
544:
(a) Complaints issued by a public officer pursuant to this article shall be served in the following manner. At least fourteen (14) days prior to the date of the hearing, the public officer shall mail copies of the complaint by certified mail or statutory overnight delivery, return receipt requested, to all interested parties whose identity and address are reasonably ascertainable. Copies of the complaint shall also be mailed by first-class mail to the property address to the attention of the occupants of the property, if any, and shall be posted on the property within three (3) business days of filing the complaint and at least fourteen (14) days prior to the date of the hearing.
(b) For interested parties whose mailing address is unknown, a notice stating the date, time, and place of the hearing shall be published in the newspaper in which the sheriff's advertisements appear in such county once a week for two (2) consecutive weeks prior to the hearing.
(c) Orders and other filings made subsequent to service of the initial complaint shall be served in the manner provided in this Code section on any interested party who answers the complaint or appears at the hearing. (Ord. of 8-9-16)
545:
(a) A notice of lis pendens shall be filed in the office of the Clerk of Superior Court of Floyd County at the time of filing the complaint in the Floyd County Magistrate Court. Such notice shall have the same force and effect as other lis pendens notices provided by law.
(b) The amount of the cost of demolition, including all court costs, appraisal fees, administrative costs incurred by the county tax commissioner or municipal tax collector or city revenue officer, and all other costs necessarily associated with the abatement action, including restoration to grade of the real property after demolition, shall be a lien against the real property upon which such cost was incurred.
(c) The lien provided for in this Code section shall attach to the real property upon the filing of a certified copy of the order requiring repair, closure or demolition in the office of the Clerk of Superior Court of Floyd County and shall relate back to the date of the filing of the lis pendens notice required under O.C.G.A. § 41-2-12(c). The clerk of Superior Court shall record and index such certified copy of the order in the deed records of Floyd County and enter the lien on the general execution docket. The lien shall be superior to all other liens on the property, except liens for taxes to which the lien shall be inferior, and shall continue in force until paid.
(d) Upon final determination of costs, fees, and expenses incurred in accordance with this article, the public officer responsible for enforcement actions in accordance with this Code section shall transmit to the appropriate county tax commissioner or the office of the Floyd County Manager who is designated as the county revenue officer and secured by said lien, together with copies of all notices provided to interested parties. The statement of the public officer shall be transmitted within ninety (90) days of completion of the repairs, demolition or closure. It shall be the duty of the appropriate county tax commissioner or municipal tax collector or city revenue officer, who is responsible or whose duties include the collection of municipal taxes, to collect the amount of the lien using all methods available for collecting real property ad valorem taxes, including specifically O.C.G.A., Title 48, Ch. 4; provided, however, that the limitation of O.C.G.A. § 48-4-78 which requires twelve (12) months of delinquency before commencing a tax foreclosure shall not apply. A county tax commissioner shall collect and enforce municipal liens imposed pursuant to this article in accordance with O.C.G.A. § 48-5-359.1. The county tax commissioner or revenue officer shall remit the amount collected to Floyd County.
(e) Enforcement of liens pursuant to this Code section may be initiated at any time following receipt by the county tax commissioner or municipal tax collector or city revenue officer of the final determination of costs in accordance with this Code section. The unpaid lien amount shall bear interest and penalties from and after the date of final determination of costs in the same amount as applicable to interest and penalties on unpaid real property ad valorem taxes. An enforcement proceeding pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 48-4-78 for delinquent ad valorem taxes may include all amounts due under this article.
(f) The redemption amount in any enforcement proceeding pursuant to this Code section shall be the full amount of the costs as finally determined in accordance with this Code section together with interest, penalties, and costs incurred by the governing authority, county tax commissioner, municipal tax collector, or city revenue officer in the enforcement of such lien. Redemption of property from the lien may be made in accordance with the provisions of O.C.G.A. §§ 48-4-80 and 48-4-81.
(g) The county may waive and release any such lien imposed on property upon the owner of such property entering into a contract with the county agreeing to a timetable for rehabilitation of the real property of the dwelling, building, or structure on the property and demonstrating the financial means to accomplish such rehabilitation.
(h) Any person affected by an order requiring the abatement of a nuisance, including the closure, repair, alteration, improvement, or demolition of a dwelling, building, or structure issued by the Floyd County Magistrate Court may petition the Superior Court of Floyd County by direct appeal under O.C.G.A. § 5-3-29.
(Ord. of 8-9-16)
546:
(a) In addition to having a dwelling, building, or structure closed pursuant to an order under this article, a public officer may bring an immediate, emergency action ordering the closing of a dwelling, building, or structure in urgent cases where such property is found to be unfit for human habitation or for commercial, industrial, or business uses. Such emergency petition may be bought prior to issuing a complaint for the abatement of a nuisance under this article.
(b) A petition requesting an emergency closing may be brought under the following conditions:
(1) After inspection of a dwelling, building, or structure, a public officer may proceed with filing an emergency petition to close the property upon finding that the dwelling, building, or structure constitutes an immediate danger to the health, safety and welfare of those persons visiting, working or residing within such dwelling, building, or structure, and that imminent harm to the occupants thereof has occurred or is likely to result from the continued use of such dwelling, building or structure.
(2) The public officer shall prepare a petition which shall identify subject real property by appropriate street address and official tax map reference; identify the owner and known residents or users of the subject property; identify the exact nature of danger and all applicable codes relevant to such danger. The complaint shall also contain a statement requesting the closure of the dwelling, building, or structure and may place such conditions as are reasonable on the opening of such property, including the repair of the dwelling, building, or structure.
(3) A hearing shall be scheduled by the Floyd County Magistrate Court as soon as practicable, given the nature of the danger and the likelihood of injury alleged in the complaint.
(4) The owner of the property and any person in possession of said property and premises shall be served personally with a copy of the complaint whenever possible. The public officer, any officer of the Floyd County Police Department, and any person authorized by the State of Georgia as a process server may attempt to make such personal service. Failure to perfect personal service shall not be cause to dismiss the complaint or postpone the hearing. Where personal service is not obtained on all of the above parties, a copy of the complaint shall be posted on the property on the date the complaint is filed, in addition, the public officer shall mail copies of the complaint by certified mail or statutory overnight delivery, return receipt requested, and by first-class mail, to the residents and owner of the property. If the case of single-family dwellings, service on one (1) adult (persons eighteen (18) years of age and over) resident of the property shall be sufficient to obtain personal service. In the case of multi-family dwellings, service must be attempted for each residential unit.
(5) If after such notice and hearing, the Floyd County Magistrate Court determines that the dwelling, building, or structure in question is unfit for human habitation or is unfit for its current commercial, industrial, or business use, is not in compliance with applicable codes, and constitutes an immediate danger to the health, safety and welfare of those persons working or residing within such dwelling, building, or structure, the court shall state in writing findings of fact in support of such determination and shall issue and cause to be served upon the owner and residents an order to close such dwelling, building, or structure. The court may place such conditions as are reasonable on the opening of such property, including the repair of the dwelling, building, or structure.
(6) Notwithstanding the foregoing, in cases where the conditions of a dwelling, building, or structure are so dangerous that a delay in closing such dwelling, building, or structure would/could cause a substantial likelihood of immediate harm or injury to those persons visiting, working or residing therein, the chief building official or the city manager may issue an order temporarily closing the property pending a hearing in the Floyd County Magistrate Court. In that event, the public officer shall proceed with filing a petition and scheduling a hearing using the provisions set forth under this Code section. Any hearing held under this paragraph (6) shall be scheduled no later than seventy-two (72) hours after the temporary closing of the property.
(7) All orders by the Floyd County Magistrate Court to close the property and all temporary orders by the chief building official or the city manager to temporarily close a property shall be binding on all persons, and failure to abide by such orders shall be a violation of this Code and is enforceable by the Floyd County Police Department or any authorized law enforcement agency. The chief building official, may, in his discretion, allow persons to temporarily enter into a closed dwelling, building, or structure for the purpose of removing personal property or to secure the dwelling, building, or structure.
(Ord. of 8-9-16)

551:
Unless the context demands otherwise, the words and terms used in sections 2-10-2 through 2-10-5 shall have the following definitions:
Alarm or alarm system: Any mechanical or electrical device which is designed or used to emit a sound or signal signifying the occurrence of an unauthorized entry, fire, or other occurrence requiring urgent attention and to which emergency units may be expected to respond.
False alarm: An alarm signal eliciting a response by police or firefighters or other public officials when a situation requiring a response by police or firefighters or other public officials does not in fact exist, excluding alarm signals caused by no fault of the user and caused by no apparent malfunction and also excluding an alarm signal caused by violent conditions of nature, such as, but not limited to, lightning, tornadoes, or other extraordinary circumstances not reasonably subject to control by the alarm business or alarm user.
False alarm penalty: An administrative fee imposed by the city/county to defray the expense to the city/county for responding to false alarms. The amount of the fees shall be as set out in the fee schedule as provided in subsection (g) of section 2-10-5.
False alarm signal: A signal indicating an emergency requiring immediate action of the fire department, including, but not limited to, an alarm from a manually operated fire alarm box, a water flow alarm or an alarm from an automatic fire/smoke detection system or device.
Fire equipment trouble alarm: An alarm indicating some form of malfunction or trouble with the fire protection or fire detecting system or device being monitored. Such trouble alarm does not indicate the need for emergency fire department response to the site, but only that the person responsible for maintenance of the system being monitored is to be notified of the trouble alarm signal.
Police signal: A signal from a manually operated or automatic device which indicates an emergency requiring immediate response by the police department.
(Ord. No. 2000-005A, § 2, 9-26-00; Ord. No. 10-24, 2023, 10-24-23)
552:
It is the purpose of sections 2-10-2 through 2-10-5 to establish requirements for the monitoring and/or receiving of fire and burglar alarm signals, and fire equipment trouble alarms at the 911 center.
(Ord. No. 2000-005A, § 2, 9-26-00; Ord. No. 10-24, 2023, 10-24-23)
553:
(a) All alarm systems must be registered within thirty (30) days of installation.
(b) Initial registration fee is fifteen dollars ($15.00) for newly installed alarm systems.
(c) Registration is not transferable. New owners must re-register and pay the fifteen-dollar fee.
(d) There will be no registration fee or fine for medical alarms.
(e) All alarm companies must submit a list of all customers in Rome and Floyd County to the E911 center annually between January 1 and January 31. The list should include the name of the customer, the customer's address and customer's phone number.
(f) Failure to register/re-register an alarm system within the allotted time will result in a fine as shown in the fee schedule.
(g) Any response to an alarm that has not been registered/re-registered will result in a fine shown in the accepted fee schedule.
(h) Alarm installation companies will be provided with and required to present a copy of the city/county alarms ordinance to each customer at the time of alarm installation.
(i) Failure of the alarm installation company to notify the customer or the central monitoring center of these requirements will result in a fine as shown in the fee schedule.
(Ord. No. 2000-005A, § 2, 9-26-00; Ord. No. 10-24, 2023, 10-24-23)
554:
(a) Connections: No emergency signal alarm shall be connected directly to the 911 center. All emergency signal alarms will be monitored by an answering center/person who will then contact the 911 center.
(b) Automatic dialers: It shall be unlawful to key automatic dialer fire or burglar alarms to the city/county emergency numbers or to the 911 center. These types of alarms shall be keyed to a private service that can then notify the 911 center.

557:
When used in this article, the following terms and phrases shall have the respective meanings ascribed to them:
Dispensing station: An independent dispensing station located on a larger gas pump which said station dispenses one (1) or more types of gas out of said station. For instance and as an example, on most of the typical pumps located today, there are three (3) stations and those stations are dispensers for unleaded gas, gas plus and super unleaded gas. Each one (1) of those dispensers is an independent station as defined herein.
Qualified attendant: A person employed by the person operating the self-service motor fuel dispensing pump present at the pump's location, to operate the pump in dispensing the fuel into the motor vehicle or other container of the member of the public seeking to obtain fuel through the pump.
Self-service motor fuel dispensing pump: A pump which dispenses gasoline, diesel fuel or any other motor fuel to members of the public, by the operation of the pump, or devices thereon, which is intended to permit the member of the general public to dispense the fuel personally, without the necessity or requirement that an attendant be present, to dispense the fuel into the motor vehicle or container of any other kind, provided by the person seeking to obtain the fuel.
Vehicle: An automobile, truck or other self-propelled vehicle using a gasoline, diesel or other internal combustion engine as the motive power for its locomotion.
(Code 1979, § 7-3021; Ord. No. 2001-003A, § 1, 7-10-01; Ord. No. 10-24, 2023, 10-24-23)
558:
It is hereby found and declared that the dispensing of gasoline and other flammable fuels, without control over the dispensing into unauthorized containers with the subsequent dangers inherent thereto; the inherent danger by use of self-service of dispensing gasoline and other fuels to minors who may lack the ability to safely transport the same and/or to other persons who are unable to safely operate a vehicle because of intoxication and for other reasons; the inherent danger to the public of the handling of a bulk flammable and combustible product in case of riots and other civil disorders during which personal and property damage are commonplace occurrences; the lack of complete control over spillage of gasoline and other fuels and oils that cause or may cause physical injury to persons while servicing their own vehicles; and the danger to life and limb by reason of spillage and improper practices near pumps unsupervised, is a present, real and serious danger and risk to the health, welfare, safety, morals, convenience, order and well-being of the citizens of the county.
(Code 1979, § 7-3022; Ord. No. 10-24, 2023, 10-24-23)
559:
It shall be unlawful for any person to operate within the county self-service motor fuel pumps which dispense gasoline, diesel fuel or other motor fuel without a qualified attendant being physically present at the self-service pump at all times unless all requirements as set out in section 2-10-23 are met by the applicant. This applies to all county self-service fuel stations where fuel is received by members of the public; and provided further that permit to operate the pump has been obtained from the clerk of the board of commissioners as prescribed herein.
(Code 1979, § 7-3023; Ord. No. 2001-003A, § 2, 7-10-01; Ord. No. 10-24, 2023, 10-24-23)
560:
(a) Any person desiring to operate a self-service motor fuel dispensing pump before installing and commencing the operation of the same, shall apply to the clerk of the board of commissioners for a permit. 2-10-63.1 Purposes and intents; organization; division of fire prevention; administration.
(a) Purposes and intents. It is the primary purpose of this article to provide for the reasonable and realistic protection of life and property from the hazards created by fire out of control, smoke, explosion, or panic created from a fear of fire out of control, smoke, or explosion. It is the basic intent of this article to accomplish its primary purpose:
(1) Through education efforts and programs designed to change high-risk attitudes and behaviors that are the root causes of most fires out of control;
(2) Through consultations and informational programs, develop in the citizens of and visitors to the City of Rome and Floyd County, an awareness of the provisions of this article, and other applicable laws, codes, and standards, and aid them to determine the options available to correct hazards, problems, or violations identified;
(3) By providing through this article reasonable, realistic, and practical safeguards against fire out of control and its related hazards; and
(4) As may be deemed necessary, initiate enforcement and legal proceedings as set forth in this article to gain compliance with the provisions of this article and the codes and standards adopted by this article.
This article is hereby declared to be remedial and shall be construed to secure the beneficial interests and purposes thereof, which are public safety, health, and general welfare, through safety to life and property from fire out of control, explosion and other hazards incident to the use and occupancy of buildings, structures, facilities, or premises located in Floyd County.
(b) Organization and programs. There is hereby created the division of fire prevention within the Rome/Floyd Fire Department for the purpose of implementing the provisions of this article. The division shall be under the direction and general supervision of the fire marshal. The fire marshal is the fire code official for the purposes of this article for Floyd County. The fire marshal is responsible to the fire chief for the administration, implementation, and enforcement of the provisions of this article and for the direction and supervision of the division. The division shall strive to improve the safety and lives and property from fire out of control and its associated hazards within Floyd County through programs of safety education, through consultations, and through the inspection of buildings, structures, facilities, and premises as often as deemed appropriate by the fire marshal and fire chief. As the fire chief and fire marshal deem appropriate, the division may develop and implement, in coordination and cooperation with other departments, agencies or organizations, public or private, a comprehensive program of community emergency education.
(c) Appointment of the fire marshal. The fire marshal shall be appointed by the fire chief based on an evaluation of the applicant's qualifications. The appointment shall continue until the fire marshal vacates the position or is removed for cause in accordance with the applicable policies and regulations of the City of Rome and Rome-Floyd Fire Department.
(d) Assistance to the fire marshal. The fire chief may detail or assign members of the Rome-Floyd Fire Department to the division of fire prevention to assist the fire marshal. Such members shall be under the direction and supervision of the fire marshal during their detail or assignment to the division. The fire chief, upon request of the fire marshal, may fill positions deemed necessary for carrying out the purposes and programs of the division, in accordance with the personnel policies and regulations of the City of Rome. The selections shall be open to members and nonmembers of the Rome-Floyd Fire Department. Employees assigned to fill positions with the division shall be under the direction and supervision of the fire marshal.
(e) Enforcement assistance. The chief of police, the building official or law enforcement officers of Floyd County shall render assistance to the fire chief or the fire marshal upon request in the implementation and enforcement of this article.
2-10-63.2 Applicability of this article and adopted codes and standards.
(a) Applicability. The provisions of this article, and the codes and standards adopted by this article, shall apply to all new and existing buildings, structures, premises, facilities and conditions within Floyd County; provided, however, existing situations or conditions not in strict compliance with this article or the codes and standards adopted by this article, and not in contravention with state law, rules or regulations, may be continued unless they are deemed by the fire marshal to constitute a distinct hazard to life or to property from fire out of control, smoke or explosion. The provisions of this article shall not apply to the interior of one-family or two-family dwellings or to premises upon which such dwellings are located or to the interior of any apartment dwelling unit, provided such dwellings or apartments are used strictly for residential purposes. This article and the codes and standards adopted by this article shall apply to such dwelling units whenever an activity coming under this article is conducted therein and/or which creates a hazard from fire out of control, smoke or explosion to life or to property.
(b) Existing and special historic buildings. The provisions of this article shall apply to existing buildings or structures in Floyd County as provided in this article. The provisions of this article shall apply to existing buildings or structures and special buildings or structures identified by the federal government, State of Georgia, Floyd County, Georgia, or by the City of Rome, Georgia, as historic buildings; provided, however, the provisions of this article shall be coordinated by the fire marshal with the applicable provisions of federal, state, and local laws or regulations, as applicable.
(c) Federal or state authority. The provisions of this article shall not be held to deprive any federal or state agency, or any applicable governing body having jurisdiction, of any power or authority which it had on the effective date of the adoption of this article or any remedy then existing for the enforcement of its orders, nor shall it deprive an individual or corporation of its legal rights as provided by law.
2-10-63.3 Administrative liability.
(a) Administrative liability. Any officer or employee of Floyd County empowered or authorized to administer or act under the provisions of this article or other applicable codes or standards in force in Floyd County or required by the State of Georgia, and acting for the county or state in the discharge of his or her duties, shall not be held liable personally, and he or she is hereby relieved from all personal liability from any damages that may accrue to any person or property as a result of any act required, implied or permitted in the discharge of his or her duties, or as required, implied or permitted by this article or other applicable codes in force in the county or adopted or required by the State of Georgia, or as a result of the omission of any action required or authorized by this article or other applicable codes in force by the county or adopted or required by the State of Georgia. Any suit instituted against any officer or employee of the Floyd County in connection with the implementation of the provisions of this Code or other applicable codes in force in Floyd County or adopted or required by the State of Georgia shall be defended by the legal representative of the Floyd County until such matter is settled.
(b) Liability. Floyd County shall not be liable for any damage to persons or property from any act or any failure to act in connection with any provision of this article or other applicable law, regulation or codes in force in the city or adopted or required by the State of Georgia.
(c) Permitting and inspection. The inspection, approval or permitting of any building or plan by any employee of the Division of Fire Prevention of the Fire Department of Floyd County, under the requirements of this article, shall not be construed in any court as a warranty of the physical condition of such building or the adequacy of such plan. Neither Floyd County nor any employee thereof shall be liable in tort for damages for any defect or hazardous or illegal condition or inadequacy in such building or plan, nor for any component of such building which may occur subsequent to such inspection, approval or permitting.
2-10-63.4 Conducting inspections; right of entry; related provisions.
(a) Inspections. The fire marshal is authorized to inspect, or cause to be inspected, as he or she deems appropriate or necessary based on fire experience in the county, on complaint, or on other applicable grounds, and as resources permit, buildings, structures, premises, and facilities coming within the scope of this article. The purpose of such inspections is to ascertain if any conditions exist which could be reasonably construed to cause a fire out of control or explosion, or that could contribute to the spread of a fire out of control or its byproducts, or to ascertain any significant nonconformance with the purposes, intents and other provisions of this article or any other applicable law, rule or regulation affecting safety to life and/or property from fire out of control, explosion or the hazards related to same. The fire marshal is authorized to apply other applicable laws and to cause to be corrected any conditions which could be reasonably construed to cause a fire out of control or explosion or that could contribute to the spread of a fire out of control, or any significant nonconformance with the purposes, intents or provisions of this article affecting safety to life and/or property from fire out of control, explosion or the hazards related to same.
(b) Right of entry to conduct inspections. The fire marshal or his or her authorized representatives may, to the extent permitted by law, have free access to and the right to enter at all reasonable times any building, structure, facility, or premises, except single-family or two-family dwellings, located within Floyd County, whether completed or under construction, for the purpose of conducting inspections and otherwise implementing the provisions of this article. Before entering any building, structure, facility, or premises not normally open to the public, except when a fire out of control or other emergency condition exists or has occurred, the fire marshal or his representatives shall obtain the consent of the occupant, owner, or person in charge at the time. Where consent to enter is refused, the fire marshal may seek an order or an administrative search warrant from the Magistrate Court of Floyd County, or if deemed appropriate, from the Superior Court of Floyd County, authorizing his or her entry or that of his or her representatives for the purpose of conducting the inspection or investigation. The term "emergency condition," for the purposes of this section, shall mean any condition or circumstance which the fire marshal or the fire chief determines to constitute an immediate threat or danger to the occupants of the building, structure, facilities or premises or to persons or property exposed to a fire out of control, the hazards associated with fire out of control, explosion, the threat of fire or explosion, or exposed to risks from some other hazardous condition or circumstances.
(c) Implied consent. Any application for, or the acceptance of, any approval, permit, license or certificate requested or required pursuant to this article, any applicable code or other applicable law or ordinance of the City of Rome or the state, constitutes agreement and consent by the person making the application, or accepting the approval, permit, license or certificate to allow the fire marshal or his or her representatives to enter the building, structure, facility or premises at any reasonable time to conduct inspections as may be deemed appropriate by the fire marshal or as otherwise provided by this article or other applicable state law or ordinance, or rules or regulations.
2-10-63.5 Notice of, or order to, eliminate dangerous or unlawful conditions.
(a) Notice of violations. Whenever the fire marshal or his or her designated representatives find any violations of this article, applicable adopted codes, or standards, or any fire hazards, as defined herein, they are authorized to issue or serve a written notice of the findings of an inspection as set forth in section 2-10-63.4 and to notify the building official. For the purposes of this article, a fire hazard means anything or act which increases or may cause an increase of the hazard or menace of fire out of control to a greater degree than that customarily recognized as normal by persons in the public service regularly engaged in preventing fires out of control; or which may obstruct, delay, hinder or interfere with the operations of the Rome-Floyd Fire Department or the egress of occupants in the event of fire out of control or other emergency condition, actual or perceived.
(b) Abatement order—Written. Whenever the fire marshal or his or her designated representatives find any violations of this article or any fire hazards, which are deemed to create a serious or significant potential for fire out of control or explosion or which are deemed to create a serious or significant potential threat to life in event of fire out of control or explosion, they are authorized to issue a written order to correct or abate the violations or hazards. Such order when issued shall set forth a reasonable and realistic time frame or date limit for correction, abatement or compliance. The time frame for correction, abatement or compliance established by or as directed by the fire marshal or his or her designated representative may be reasonably correlated by him or her or them to the seriousness or relative degree of hazard, and/or to the complexity of the means of correction or abatement.
(c) Abatement order—Verbal. Where deemed necessary, due to the potential risk to life or property, the fire marshal or his or her representative may issue a verbal order for the immediate correction or abatement of a violation or fire hazard. This may be followed by a written order of notice or action.
(d) Summary abatement. The fire marshal or the fire chief shall have the authority to summarily abate any violation of this article or any fire hazard, which constitutes an immediate or imminent danger or threat to life in their judgment, and where the following of the provisions for obtaining corrective action or abatement as set forth elsewhere in this article is not practical in their judgment.
(e) Unsafe buildings or structures. Any building or structure which is deemed to be structurally unsafe or which is not provided with adequate means of egress, or which is deemed to constitute a serious fire hazard, or which is otherwise deemed dangerous to human life, or which in relation to existing use constitutes a hazard to the safety, health or welfare to the public by reason of inadequate maintenance, dilapidation, obsolescence, fire damage, disaster damage, vandalism, flood damage or abandonment, as specified in this article or by any other applicable codes or ordinances in force in Floyd County, is deemed to be an unsafe building or structure.
2-10-63.6 Serving notices or orders.
(a) Generally. The service of notices or orders issued in connection with [subsections] 2-10-63.5(a) and 2-10-63.5(b) of this article may be made by the fire marshal or his or her representatives upon the owner, occupant or person in charge of the building, structure, facility, premises or portion thereof where the hazards or violations were found, or by delivering a copy of the notice or order to any or all of the persons noted. If such person(s) cannot be served by delivery as noted, service may be accomplished by affixing a copy of the notice or order in a conspicuous place at or near the entrance of the building, structure, facility or premises, or by delivering or sending a copy of the notice or order to the known agent of the owner or occupant, or in the event of an absentee owner with no known agent, by sending a copy by certified or registered mail to the owner's last known residence, business or post office address.
(b) To occupants of certain premises. If the building, structure, facility or premises is owned by one (1) or more persons and is occupied by one (1) or more other persons under lease or otherwise, the notice or order issued in connection with this section shall apply to the occupants thereof, except where the notice or order requires the addition to or changes in the building, structure or premises such as would immediately become real estate and become the property of the owners and not the occupants unless it is otherwise agreed between or among the owners and the occupants.
2-10-63.7 Penalty provisions.
(a) General penalty; separate violations. Any person who shall fail to comply with an order of correction or abatement as set forth in this section, or who shall build or act in violation of this article or of any detailed statement of specifications or plans submitted and approved under authority of this article in connection with any approval, certificate, or permit issued thereunder, or who shall perform any act deemed to create a serious potential for fire out of control, or explosion and for which the issuance of an order to correct or abate is not adequate, and who is found guilty shall be guilty of a violation of this article. A person found guilty under this section shall, for each violation and noncompliance, respectively, be subject to punishment by a fine of not less than one hundred dollars ($100.00), nor more than five thousand dollars ($5,000.00), or by imprisonment for a period of not more than one hundred twenty (120) days or by both such fine and imprisonment. The imposition of a penalty for any violation shall not excuse the violation or permit it to continue, and the responsible persons shall correct or abate such violation within a time limit as ordered by the court. When not otherwise specified, each five (5) days a prohibited condition or violation continues following an order of the court to correct or abate the same shall constitute a separate offense.
(b) Procedures upon determination of violation—Generally. When the fire marshal, the fire chief or their authorized representatives determine that violations of this Code warrant the filing of charges or action of the court as provided for in [subsection] 2-10-63.7(a), the issuing of a citation of charges and/or summons to appear before the Magistrate Court of Floyd County shall be served by any certified law enforcement officer of Floyd County upon request of the fire marshal, the fire chief or their authorized representative.
(c) Same—Injunctive relief. In addition to the filing of charges as specified in [subsections] 2-10-63.7(a) and 2-10-63.7(b), or as a separate remedy at law, the fire marshal or the fire chief may seek injunctive relief for any fire hazard, violation, or condition that threatens the safety of life or property based on the provisions of this Code or any applicable code or ordinance of Floyd County or of the State of Georgia.
(d) Removal of prohibited conditions. The application of penalties by the court as provided for in [section] 2-10-63.7 shall not be held to prevent the enforced removal of prohibited conditions or violations.
(e) Whenever in this Code any act is prohibited or is made or declared to be unlawful or an offense, or whenever in such Code the doing of any act is required or the failure to do any act is declared to be unlawful, where no specific penalty is provided therefor, the violation of any such provision of this Code shall be punished as authorized by section 2-1-8 of the Code of Ordinances of Floyd County, Georgia.
2-10-63.8 Removal of notices or order; illegal use of buildings.
(a) Removal, generally. It shall be unlawful for any person to remove any notice or order issued in connection with this article and affixed to a building, structure, facility, or premises, without the approval of the fire marshal or his or her authorized representative.
(b) Unlawful use of building or facility. It shall be unlawful for any person to use a building, structure, facility, or premises in violation of the provisions of this article where an order has been affixed to same prohibiting the use of same under authority of any provisions of this article without the approval of the fire marshal or his or her authorized representative or the court.
(c) Change of occupancy or use of building. When it is determined that the occupancy or use of a building has changed from that shown on the certificate of occupancy issued by the building official, the fire marshal, or the state fire marshal, the fire marshal may issue such notice or orders as necessary and in conformance with this article to remove or remedy any noted violations or hazards, and he or she shall refer the building to the building official, or as appropriate, the state fire marshal, for any repairs, alterations, remodeling, removing or demolition required.
2-10-63.9 Coordination with and application of related codes and standards.
(a) Changes in existing buildings or facilities. Any alterations, additions or changes required in existing buildings, structures, facilities, or premises because of a change in use, occupancy, exit design or other reason shall be made in compliance with the codes and standards adopted under this article and as set for in section 2-10-1 and 2-10-64 of this chapter.
(b) Review of plans coordinated. The fire marshal and the building official shall coordinate their review of plans on new construction and/or renovations or alterations of existing buildings or structures so as to ascertain compliance with this article and the codes and standards adopted by this article under their respective jurisdictions. The building official, pursuant to state, shall not issue any building permit on buildings under the jurisdiction of the state fire marshal (O.C.G.A. §§ 25-2-13 and 25-2-14), until the required state construction permit is issued by the state fire marshal.
(c) New construction. The fire marshal and the building official shall have the authority to jointly consider and approve a modification of any of the applicable codes for new construction with regard to matters relating to fire protection and safety to life in the event of fire out of control or related emergencies where the proposed designed, fire protection system, building use, or construction method involved is unusual or where it involves an unusual hazard, condition, or hardship, and the provisions of the codes and standards in force do not clearly or adequately deal with the proposed design, protection system application or design, building use, or construction method, in their judgment. Such approvals shall not result in a condition(s) that is/are less protective than any code or standard adopted by the state.
(d) Alternate materials. It is the intent of this provision to allow the use of designs, systems, methods, or devices of equivalent or superior quality, strength, fire resistance, effectiveness, durability, and safety to those prescribed by the applicable codes and standards, provided that technical documentation, data, or other information or material acceptable to the fire marshal and building official is submitted for review and such demonstrates to their satisfaction the equivalency of the design, system, method, or device for the intended use. Any modification or alternate safeguard jointly approved by the fire marshal and the building official shall not afford a condition less safe to life, and where appropriate, property, than in their judgment would be provided with compliance with the provisions of applicable codes or standards.
2-10-63.10 Modifications and appeals.
(a) Existing conditions. The fire marshal shall have the authority to modify any of the provisions of the adopted codes or standards adopted by reference by this article, except regarding buildings under the jurisdiction of O.C.G.A. § 25-2-13, upon application in writing by the owners and/or occupants of an existing building, structure, facility or premises, or by their authorized agents, when there are practical difficulties in the way of carrying out the strict letter of this Code or the codes or standards adopted by reference by this article or Floyd County.
