2-10-63.11 General provisions.
(a) Interference with fire officials. It shall be unlawful for any person to interfere with, abuse, or obstruct in any way the fire chief, the fire marshal, or their representatives in carrying out any actions in accordance with their official duties as set forth by this article, or by any other applicable local ordinance, or by any law or regulation of the State of Georgia.
(b) Unlawful use of credentials; unlawful impersonation of fire official. It shall be unlawful for any unauthorized person to use an official or unofficial badge or credential so as to impersonate an authorized fire official or to otherwise impersonate a fire official.
(c) Authority to investigate fires, explosions, false alarms or related incidents. The fire chief, the fire marshal or his authorized representatives are authorized to investigate the cause, origin and circumstances of any fire or explosion, or to investigate any incident resulting from the sending or sounding of a false alarm of fire or a bomb threat. When, in the judgment of the fire marshal, reasonable cause exists that a fire or explosion may have been of criminal origin, the fire marshal or his or her authorized representative is authorized to locate and take custody of any and all physical evidence relating to the cause of the fire or explosion and to continue the investigation to the extent deemed appropriate within the limits of division resources and within the limits of applicable state laws. The fire marshal shall inform the Floyd County Police Department of each fire of criminal or suspected criminal origin, false alarms, or bomb threats. The fire marshal shall also assist the Floyd County Police Department in its investigations of reported incidents, if so, requested by that department. The Floyd County Police Department shall be responsible for the investigation of fires and/or explosions of criminal or suspected criminal origin, false alarms or bomb threats so as to identify, apprehend and assist in the prosecution of the persons responsible for such criminal acts.
(d) Evacuation of buildings, structures, facilities or premises. When, in the judgment of the fire chief, the fire marshal, or their authorized representatives in their absence, there is an actual or serious potential danger to the occupants of or persons in close proximity to any building, structure, facility or premises because of unsafe structural conditions, or the presence of explosives, explosive fumes or vapor, toxic fumes, gases or materials, the fire chief, the fire marshal, or their authorized representatives in their absence, may order the complete or partial immediate evacuation of any building, structure, facility or premises and, as necessary, areas in such proximity to these as to be endangered. All persons under order to evacuate shall promptly leave the evacuation area and shall not reenter until authorized to do so by the official who issued the evacuation order. This section shall not pertain to bomb threats where no bomb or explosive device is known to exist. In such bomb threat situations, the decision to evacuate or not to evacuate is the responsibility of the person in charge of the building, structure, facility or premises at that time.
(e) Permits and approvals. A person shall not maintain, store, or handle materials, or conduct processes which produce conditions hazardous to life or property, or install equipment used in connection with such activities without first obtaining approval, or as appropriate based on the provisions of section 2-10-63.12 of this article, a permit from the fire marshal. Where conditions or activities are also regulated by a state or federal agency and a permit, license or certificate is required by the regulating agency, then no local permit is required; provided, however, the approval of the fire marshal is required, and he/she shall have the authority to apply the provisions of this article where a hazardous condition is discovered.
(f) Tests. All equipment required by this article or other applicable codes adopted by Floyd County or by the State of Georgia shall be maintained in a safe, sound, and operational condition. The fire marshal may require tests or test reports as proof of compliance. Required tests and reports are to be made at the expense of the owner or his agent by an approved testing laboratory or other approval agency or firm acceptable to the fire marshal.
(g) Authority to expose or stop work. Whenever any construction or installation coming under this article is subject to inspection prior to use and is covered or concealed without having first been inspected, the fire marshal may require by verbal and/or written order that such work be exposed for inspection. The fire marshal shall be notified when the installation is ready for inspection within a reasonable period. When any construction or installation work is being performed in violation of the plans, specifications or understandings as approved by the fire marshal, a written order may be issued to the responsible person to stop work on that portion of the work which is in violation. The order shall state the nature of the violation. No work shall be continued on that portion until the violation has been corrected and the order is lifted by the fire marshal or his or her designated representative.
(h) Effect of court decision. If, for any reason, any provision, section, subsection, clause or phrase of this article, or any code or standard adopted by reference by this article, is held to be invalid or unconstitutional by a decision of a court of competent jurisdiction, such decision shall not affect the validity of the remaining provisions of this article, or of any code or standard adopted by reference by this article.

The execution shall be a lien on the property, and when recorded in the general execution docket of Floyd County, shall be a lien on all property of the defendant in execution from the date of such recording.
(Ord. No. 2006-003A, § 6, 7-25-06)
609:
The notice, described in subsection 2-11-24(b), shall contain a demand for removal within three (3) days, and the notice shall advise that upon failure to comply with the notice to remove, Floyd County shall undertake such removal with the cost being levied against the owner of such vehicle and that said nuisance will be declared a violation of the Code of Floyd County and shall be punished as provided for in sections 2-11-3 and 2-11-8.
(Ord. No. 2006-003A, § 7, 7-25-06)
610:
If the violation cited in the notice has not been remedied within the notice period for compliance, Floyd County shall have the right to take possession of the junked vehicle or abandoned motor vehicle and remove it from the public property where it is located. It shall be unlawful for any persons to interfere with, hinder, or refuse to allow such person or persons acting for Floyd County to remove said vehicle under the provisions of this chapter.
(Ord. No. 2006-003A, § 8, 7-25-06)
611:
Within forty-eight (48) hours of the removal of the vehicle, Floyd County shall give notice to the registered owner of the vehicle, if known, that said vehicle, (or vehicles) has been impounded and stored for violation of this chapter. The notice shall give the location of the vehicle (or vehicles) and the amount of costs incurred by Floyd County for removal and that said vehicle is subject to sale pursuant to this chapter.
(Ord. No. 2006-003A, § 9, 7-25-06)
612:
Upon removing a vehicle under the provisions of section 2-11-27, Floyd County shall after ten (10) days appraise said vehicle. If the vehicle is appraised at one thousand dollars ($1,000.00) or less, Floyd County shall execute an affidavit so attesting and describe the vehicle, including the license plates, if any, and stating the location and appraised value of the vehicle. Floyd County, after complying with the above, may summarily dispose of the vehicles and execute a certificate of sale. If the vehicle is appraised at over one thousand dollars ($1,000.00), Floyd County shall be authorized to sell the abandoned vehicle at public auction.
(Ord. No. 2006-003A, § 10, 7-25-06)
613:
Any abandoned motor vehicle or junked vehicle sold at public sale by Floyd County shall be sold to the highest and best bidder. At the time of payment of the purchase price, Floyd County shall execute a certificate of sale in duplicate, the original of which shall be given to the purchaser, and a copy thereof to be maintained in the files of Floyd County pertaining to the pubic sale of personal property items. Should the sale for any reason be declared invalid by a court of competent jurisdiction, Floyd County's liability shall be limited to the return of the purchase price.
(Ord. No. 2006-003A, § 11, 7-25-06)
614:
The owner of any vehicle seized under the provisions of this chapter may redeem such vehicle at any time after its removal but prior to the sale or destruction thereof upon proof of ownership and payment to Floyd County of such sum as it may determine and fix for the actual expense of removal, and any preliminary sale advertising expenses, the costs incurred by Floyd County, if any, for storage for each vehicle redeemed.
(Ord. No. 2006-003A, § 12, 7-25-06)
615:
During the impoundment of any abandoned motor vehicle or junked vehicle removed from public property pursuant to this chapter and prior to the sale of any such vehicle, should any person assert that he is a lien holder on said vehicle or should any lien holder be identified by research into the ownership of said vehicle by any agent of Floyd County, then said lien holder shall receive any notice required by this chapter to be delivered to any owner of any said vehicle. Any such lien holder may obtain possession of the vehicle from Floyd County by paying off costs as described in section 2-11-31 above at any time prior to the sale of said vehicle as set out in this chapter.
(Ord. No. 2006-003A, § 13, 7-25-06)
616:
(a) Upon information made known to the sheriff of Floyd County, and/or chief of police of Floyd County, or to any officer of the sheriff's department or the county police department, or the county attorney, that any person is in violation of this article, the one gaining the information shall cause a citation to be issued requiring such person to appear before the judge of the magistrate court on a day and time certain, then and there to stand trial for violation of this article.
(b) Citations issued hereunder shall be pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 15-10-63 and shall be personally served upon the person accused. Each citation shall state the time and place at which the accused is to appear for trial.
(Ord. No. 2006-003A, § 14, 7-25-06)
617:
This chapter shall not be the exclusive regulation of abandoned or junked vehicles within Floyd County and shall be supplemental and in addition to the other ordinances, statutes or provisions of law hereto or hereinafter enacted by Floyd County, the state, or other legal entity or agency having jurisdiction.
(Ord. No. 2006-003A, § 15, 7-25-06)

620:

County vehicle means any automobile, truck, van, or other motor vehicle designed primarily for on-the-road use which is owned or otherwise under the exclusive control of Floyd County, Georgia.

Tobacco product means any kind or type of tobacco, whether loose leaf, processed or rolled, intended, packaged or sold for the purpose of chewing, dipping, smoking, vapes, electronic cigarette, e-juice, wax vape pens and herbal vaporizers unless the vaporizers are medically prescribed by a licensed MD for breathing assistance.
(Amend. of 5-10-94, § 1, Ord. No. 2015-005A, 12-8-15)
621:
This article is enacted for the purpose of preserving and protecting the public health, safety and welfare by reducing individual exposure to first- and secondhand tobacco smoke, by reducing the possibility of fire in county facilities and by providing a generally more healthful and sanitary environment for working and for conducting public business.
(Amend. of 5-10-94, § 1)
622:
No person shall smoke or otherwise use any tobacco product while in any county facility. After consultation with the appropriate department head(s), the county manager may establish reasonable work rule restrictions governing smoking and the use of tobacco products in non-enclosed or outdoor employee work areas and upon the grounds of county facilities frequented by members of the general public. The county manager shall cause the erection and installation of signs necessary and appropriate to promote the purposes of this article.
(Amend. of 5-10-94, § 1)
623:
The sheriff of the county is authorized to designate one (1) or more specific locations within the confinement area of the county jail as a smoking area. The warden of the county correctional institute is authorized to designate one (1) or more specific locations within the confinement area of the correctional institute as a smoking area. Nothing in this section shall be construed to authorize smoking in any area of such jail or correctional institute which is accessible to members of the general public. The restrictions set forth in this article shall not be applicable to buildings or other structures owned by the county but under lease to private individuals or for-profit business organizations.
(Amend. of 5-10-94, § 1)
624:
No smoking or other use of tobacco products shall be permitted in any county vehicle.
(Amend. of 5-10-94, § 1)
625:

Jurisdiction shall be in the magistrate court of the county.
(Amend. of 5-10-94, § 1)
628:
As used in this article, a "political sign" is any sign, banner, pennant, valance or display constructed of cloth, canvas, light fabric, cardboard, wallboard, plywood or other light material, with or without frames, which advertises or promotes any candidate for election or any political issue which will be submitted to the voters at an election.
(Code 1979, § 6-4001; Ord. of 1-13-87; Ord. of 6-14-88)
629:
Upon information being made known to the clerk of the board of commissioners that any violation of this article is occurring, the clerk shall cause a notice to be issued requiring the violator to appear before the clerk on a day and time certain.
(Code 1979, § 6-4009; Ord. of 1-13-87; Ord. of 6-14-88)
630: Editor's note— Section 2-11-52, regulating time limitations on political signs, derived from Code 1979, § 6-4002, and ordinances adopted Jan. 13, 1987, and Mar. 15, 1988, and § 2-11-53, regulating size limitations, derived from Code 1979, § 6-4003, and an ordinance adopted Jan. 13, 1987, were repealed by § 1 of an ordinance adopted June 14, 1988.
631:
(a) Public property: No political sign shall be located upon a public street, alley, sidewalk, right-of-way, easement or other governmental property or property dedicated to a public use, except that signs attached to a wall, fence or building may project over such areas a distance not greater than six (6) inches. Political signs must be set back a minimum of ten (10) feet from the pavement of any street or public right-of-way.
(b) Obstructions: No political sign shall prevent or interfere with free ingress to or egress from any door, window or fire escape.
(c) Traffic safety: No political sign shall be located or maintained in such a place or in such a manner as to constitute a hazard to the safety of pedestrians or vehicular traffic. Political signs shall not be attached to street signs or any sign directing or controlling traffic, nor to any pole or post supporting such signs. The decision of the county traffic engineer as to whether a sign constitutes such a hazard shall be conclusive.
(d) State law: All state laws as provided for in O.C.G.A. § 21-1-1, and its modifications, and all other applicable state law must be complied with.
(Code 1979, § 6-4004; Ord. of 1-13-87; Ord. of 6-14-88, § 1)
632:
(a) Prior to posting or erecting any political sign, the candidate, the candidate's representative or the person or organization intending to post signs for or against a ballot measure, shall post a cash bond of one hundred dollars ($100.00) with the clerk of the board of commissioners. Only one (1) such bond is required for any candidate for election or for the respective proponents or opponents to a ballot measure. The amount of the bond may be returned to the person who posted it when the building inspection department certifies to the county clerk that the respective signs erected by or on behalf of the person posting the bond have not been erected or maintained in violation of this article.
(b) If any political signs shall be erected or maintained in violation of the provisions of this article, by or on behalf of the person posting the bond, the cash bond shall be forfeited.
(c) If it becomes necessary for the county to remove any political sign from private property for noncompliance with this article, and the owner of such sign desires to retrieve it from the county, a service charge of twenty-five dollars ($25.00) will be made. The county may deduct the service charge or any other charges equal to the cost of removal of the sign from the cash bond and remit the balance of such bond to the person who posted it.
(d) No bond is required where an individual erects a political sign on property owned or occupied by such person if the other provisions of this article are complied with.
(Code 1979, § 6-4005; Ord. of 1-13-87; Ord. of 6-14-88, § 1)
633:
Any person violating the terms of this article, or rules and regulations promulgated pursuant thereto, will forfeit any and all cash bonds required under section 2-11-55.
(Code 1979, § 6-4010; Ord. of 1-13-87; Ord. of 6-14-88, § 1)
634:
It is unlawful for any person to erect or maintain a political sign, other than as authorized by this article, or for any owner of real property to permit, allow, acquiesce in, sanction or condone the erection or maintenance of a political sign on such person's property other than as authorized by this article.
(Code 1979, § 6-4006; Ord. of 1-13-87; Ord. of 6-14-88, § 1)
